Rows come from the ytpost lane (python video-creation/longform-edited/graph/run.py ytpost), which picks this queue when the live video is on this channel, for a longform-edited or a longform-presentation video (Mike, 2026-11-17). Slide images live in schedule-tweets/images/ai-yt/. Status flow: 'pending' (queued) -> 'posted' (posted_at and post_url set). The JS post-yt-community.js posts only the crypto channel: never run it for this file. Shown on the dashboard's AI YouTube Posts tab.

posts.topic: Promo carousel for the live video "Evals in Production: Turning Human Verdicts Into a Score"
posts.body_style: watch-the-full-video link + headline + two arrow points + hashtags
posts.body:
▶ Watch the full video: https://youtu.be/U26NDilqCDo

Every keep or kill at my human gate is now an eval score

→ 98 clips judged on record, 82.7 percent precision
→ 11 of 17 kills were one half of a full clip and impact cut pair

#AIEngineering #LLMEvals #LangGraph

images.slide_text: Human verdicts into a score
Two kinds of harness / An agent harness runs the loop and hands the model its tools. An evaluation harness runs the evals end to end and adds up the results.
One graph, 14 steps
Rules live in the code / A rule that only lives in the context is a request. The prompt explains the job. The code enforces the rules.
The fix had three parts
A score moves by itself / 83.3 / Same prompt, same transcript, same model. The difference was one impact cut.
What the record shows / 82.7% / 184 lines covering 21 livestreams, every keep or kill on record.
The finding I didn't expect
Opinions become replays / Can a cheaper model pick as well? That used to be an opinion. Now it's a replay.
Watch the full video / Evals in Production: Turning Human Verdicts Into a Score

posts.topic: Promo carousel for the live video "How I'd Run My LangGraph Agent Pipeline on AWS"
posts.body_style: watch-the-full-video link + headline + two arrow points + hashtags
posts.body:
▶ Watch the full video: https://youtu.be/joUlFD5Xe3A

How I'd move a 7-agent LangGraph pipeline from one PC to AWS

→ A 9-hour human gate survives an 8-hour AgentCore session
→ EC2 runs only the heavy work, on Spot at up to 90% off

#AIEngineering #LangGraph #AWS

images.slide_text: My LangGraph pipeline on AWS
Today it runs on one PC / The graph and its checkpoints, 7 agents in Claude Code, one browser for images, Whisper on my GPU, the renders.
Layer 1, ingest
A gate longer than a session / 9 / An AgentCore Runtime session lasts up to 8 hours. So the graph saves state to DynamoDB, and my approval resumes it in a new session.
The agents on Bedrock
No browser, no lock / One browser was busy 3.9 hours of the build. On AWS, an image model on Bedrock, and the 7 shorts stop taking turns.
Does it run on EC2? / 90% / Yes, but only the heavy work. AWS Batch starts servers when a job arrives, and every step skips what's done.
The renders fan out / Remotion Lambda splits one render across up to 200 Lambda functions. Remotion's example: a 10-minute HD video for around 10 cents.
What changes is around it
Watch the full video / How I'd Run My LangGraph Agent Pipeline on AWS
